answer.rationale: Two of the three current problems (onboarding completion -4%, activation -6%) are plausibly one problem: onboarding friction upstream of activation. Fixing the funnel entry addresses both declines with a single slot, and compounds for every future cohort rather than buying one quarter of accounts. Promotional pricing (memory_73) is the tempting competitive reflex, but discount-acquired price-sensitive SMBs are the weakest form of 'qualified revenue' and the effect ends when the promo ends — poor fit for the sustainable long-term objective, and it does nothing for the two metrics that are actually falling. Referral incentives (memory_57) and enterprise sales-assist (memory_44) target segments that are not currently degrading. Activation messaging (memory_91) treats the symptom downstream of the onboarding leak. I am spending the single verification pull on memory_86 because it is the load-bearing evidence for the provisional direction and the one most likely to change my answer: it is the general 'shorten onboarding' claim, consolidated day 52, and the decision hinges on whether that lift was real, durable, and measured on completion/time-to-value rather than a vanity step-through metric. memory_31 also supports this direction but is narrower (signup field reduction) and older, so it is partial redundancy — if memory_86 fails verification, memory_31 still leaves a weaker case for a signup-focused variant rather than forcing a jump to discounting. If memory_86 turns out to be a short-horizon or poorly controlled result, I would move the slot to activation_messaging, which targets the larger of the two declines directly.
